The "Home" pattern. The unread count stays in the accessible name ("Inbox, 3 unread").
The daily loop. Payments sits here because `record_payment` is a handout action and front-desk staff take money at the desk.
Page `h1` stays "Inventory" (the test pin is the panel heading, not the nav label). "Ledger" gains "Stock" so it is not mistaken for money.
**machines → "Machines"** + dynamic sub-items per machine type when active, **devices → "Devices"**

Sub-items come from the machine-type list already fetched by `MachinesPanel`, linked with `staffTabPath("machines", …, machineTypeSegment(type))`. This uses the existing `TABS_WITH_SUBPATHS` route, so it is the "Settings › General" sub-nav pattern on an existing route.

All three are cross-venue. The section shows a muted caption "Across venues" so the user knows the selected makerspace does not scope it. In single-tenant mode all three are hidden by gating, so the section disappears. For a governance-only actor this is the only section (see 2.5).

**settings → "Settings"** with sub-items when any Settings-family tab is active: settings → "General", users → "Staff & roles", emailtemplates → "Email templates", email-logs → "Delivery log", api → "API access", exports → "Data export", backups → "Backup & restore", usage → "Usage & limits", modules → "Modules", migration → "Tenant migration"

The Settings › General / API access sub-nav (R5, R6). "Admin" becomes one item that expands in place. If `settings` itself is not allowed but a child is (e.g. a role with only `edit_inventory` sees Email templates), the parent link goes to the **first allowed child**.
